put:
      description: |
        Creates a new dashboard with the given ID if none exists, or replaces the complete state of an
        existing one.

        > warn
        > This is a full replacement. Any panels not included in the request body are permanently
        > removed. To make targeted changes, retrieve the current state first with
        > GET /api/dashboards/{id}, apply your changes, and submit the full updated object.

        You can optionally include `access_control.access_mode` to change the dashboard access mode.
        If the authenticated user is not authorized to change access mode for the target dashboard,
        the request returns a `403` response with a descriptive `message`.
      operationId: put-dashboards-id
      parameters:
        - description: A required header to protect against CSRF attacks
          in: header
          name: kbn-xsrf
          required: true
          schema:
            example: 'true'
            type: string
        - description: The unique ID of the dashboard to be created or updated
          in: path
          name: id
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Kibana_HTTP_APIs_kbn-dashboard-data'
      responses:
        '200':
          content:
            application/json:
              examples:
                updateDashboardResponse:
                  description: |
                    The complete updated dashboard state after a full replacement. Note that `meta.created_at` is not returned in update responses - use the GET endpoint to retrieve it.
                  summary: Update dashboard response
                  value:
                    data:
                      options:
                        auto_apply_filters: true
                        hide_panel_borders: false
                        hide_panel_titles: false
                        sync_colors: false
                        sync_cursor: true
                        sync_tooltips: false
                        use_margins: true
                      panels:
                        - config:
                            content: |-
                              ## Web logs overview

                               

                              Created with the [Dashboards API](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/kibana) using the Kibana sample web logs dataset (`kibana_sample_data_logs`). Contains:
                              - This markdown panel
                              - 2 metrics, showing request count and average response size
                              - A line chart based on an ES|QL query

                               

                               

                              [Learn more about dashboards](https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/dashboards)
                          grid:
                            h: 15
                            w: 24
                            x: 0
                            'y': 0
                          id: a1b2c3d4-0001-4000-8000-000000000001
                          type: markdown
                        - config:
                            data_source:
                              index_pattern: kibana_sample_data_logs
                              time_field: timestamp

content.text:
I made both changes in place and checked each one afterwards.

1. **'Site health' dashboard:** I added a third panel called "Requests by host". It's a bar chart counting requests for each `host.keyword` value, showing the top 10 hosts. It uses the same 'Kibana Sample Data Logs' data view and style as the "Requests by response code" panel. It sits full-width under the two existing panels, which I didn't touch. Reading the dashboard back shows 3 panels.
2. **'Server errors' rule:** The rule was disabled, and I've enabled it. Reading it back shows `enabled: true`, with status `pending` because it hasn't run yet since being turned on.
